rationale: The route REACTION→USER→CONVERSATION_MEMBERSHIP→CONVERSATION correctly represents the prompt's two-condition test (reaction on a specific message AND reactor's membership in #product-growth). The resolution_mode 'absent' is justified: the base seed's only existing reaction on the OOM alert message (1706110000.000100) is by the agent bot, who is not a #product-growth member (confirmed absent from channel_members for C_GROWTH). The design's negative roles (Kenji, Priya) describe planned reaction rows to be added by the compiler on distinct, unrelated messages (Tokyo stats in #product-growth, memory-pressure in #core-infra) — both already-anchored real messages in the base seed, and the corresponding membership rows already exist in channel_members, so these are legitimate future additions rather than contradictions of the seed. This properly stresses both failure modes (right message/wrong membership vs. right membership/wrong message) without leaking the answer. The access plan uses real, visible-ID-based API calls (conversations.history, reactions.get, conversations.members) with no hidden-field dependency. Answer attributes (reaction_type, user_id, message_id) are bare, real, retrievable columns, matching the 'absent' read-only obligation. The prompt is concise, plausible, and channel/entity references (#product-growth vs. the unrelated #growth channel) are correctly disambiguated against the seed. No mechanical or semantic defects found; the design has strong negative coverage for a bare-retrieval absent case.
